title: What repeats in these buildings, and what does not in clouds?
description: A famous monument, a temple tower and a picture of clouds are each cut by an imagined line down the middle, and the left side is compared with the right. Keeko doubts that clouds can have symmetry just because they look pretty.
teaching_notes: One idea: a figure has symmetry when a part repeats in a definite pattern, and we test it by comparing the two sides of a line down the middle. Watch for students who call a picture symmetrical because it looks beautiful or balanced.

source: Look at the pictures of the Taj Mahal and the Gopuram (a temple tower). What are the symmetries that you see in these beautiful structures? Why is the picture of the clouds not symmetrical?
video_script.why: The child learns that symmetry means a part repeating in a definite pattern, and that a picture can be lovely without any pattern.
video_script.substitution: Imagine a line down the middle of each picture and compare the left side with the right side.
video_script.anchor: The book's pictures of a famous monument, a temple tower (gopuram) and a picture of clouds
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the clouds are symmetrical because they look balanced and pretty. A line down the middle of the clouds shows that nothing on one side matches the other.
video_script.payoff_line: Where a part repeats in a definite pattern, there is symmetry.

final_answer.value: buildings: symmetry, parts repeat; clouds: no symmetry
final_answer.spoken: the two buildings have symmetry because their parts repeat, but the clouds do not

names.{{NAME_2}}: the monument shown at the chapter opening as a symmetric structure

never_show: the verdict before the answer beat
maths_rules: Symmetry: a part or parts of a figure repeat in a definite pattern.
The monument and the temple tower: a vertical line down the middle, the left side matches the right side, and parts such as towers and tiers repeat.
The clouds: no part repeats in a pattern, so no symmetry.
Test: compare the left side with the right side of a line down the middle.
video_script.design: One idea: symmetry is a part repeating in a definite pattern. Assumes the child has seen the chapter pictures. Wrong idea: a pretty picture is symmetrical. The three book pictures stay in view throughout.
